projects.title: GovAssist
projects.description: A versioned public-policy assistant that applies deterministic checks, verifies its output, and returns cited evidence instead of unsupported answers.
projects.decision: We selected GovAssist because it gives each team member a clear technical responsibility and supports a complete source-to-answer demonstration.

projects.title: Lost and Found Portal
projects.description: A controlled lost-and-found workflow with structured reports, transparent match ranking, claim verification, notifications, and one recorded handover per item.
projects.decision: We did not select this proposal because similar campus reporting methods already exist and adoption would be difficult to prove.

projects.title: Placement Readiness Platform
projects.description: A placement-readiness system that maps skill evidence to versioned company criteria, identifies eligibility gaps, and builds focused roadmaps.
projects.decision: We did not select this proposal because access to reliable company criteria and placement data is uncertain.

projects.title: Semester Workload Balancer
projects.description: A workload-forecasting and constraint-aware planning tool that detects overloaded weeks and moves only work that can be completed earlier.
projects.decision: We did not select this proposal because the workload forecast depends on historical effort data that we would first need to collect.

planningPresentation.title: Planning Presentation v1
planningPresentation.changeSummary: First submitted version. It compares four ideas and records why we chose GovAssist.
planningPresentation.description: This page contains our first planning presentation and the supporting notes for the project review.
planningPresentation.scope: GovAssist helps citizens and small businesses check selected public-scheme and tax rules. For the first version, users can enter details manually, choose an ITR use case, and check two schemes. If the available rule does not support an answer, the system shows the official source instead.
objectives: Show the result, the reason, and the source used.
Keep earlier rule versions so a result can be checked later.
Do not show a final answer when the source does not support it.
Limit the personal information stored from uploaded documents.
functions: Rule category selection and fact extraction
Verification, confidence, and cited answer output
Rule version management and change history
intendedUsers: Individuals choosing an appropriate ITR form
Small businesses interpreting selected public rules

architecture.title: Frontend
architecture.description: Pages for entering details, uploading a document, viewing the result and source, and managing rule records.

architecture.title: Application API
architecture.description: Handles sign-in, validation, rule selection, permissions, and communication between the website and stored data.

architecture.title: Rules and verification
architecture.description: Runs the selected rule version, attaches the relevant clause, and rejects a result when the evidence is not sufficient.

architecture.title: Data and files
architecture.description: Stores users, rule versions, change records, and uploaded files with separate access controls.

qualityGoals.title: Performance
items: A normal rule check should return in under 3 seconds
Limit document size and processing time
Keep page assets small and cacheable

qualityGoals.title: Security
items: Give each role only the access it needs
Use HTTPS and keep secrets out of frontend code

qualityGoals.title: Reliability
items: Show no result when evidence is insufficient
Record which rule version produced each result
Keep a record of important admin changes

qualityGoals.title: Maintainability
items: Add automated tests for rules and APIs
Document how rules and presentations are published

risks.risk: A rule changes after we publish it
risks.response: Store its effective date and add a new version instead of replacing the old one.

risks.risk: A document is sensitive or difficult to read
risks.response: Validate uploads, store only what is needed, and allow manual input as a fallback.

risks.risk: The source does not support a clear answer
risks.response: Do not show a decision. Link the user to the official source.

risks.risk: An external service reaches its free limit
risks.response: Set usage limits and keep a manual-input path that does not require OCR.
